title: Efficiency of Continuous-Time Quantum Monte Carlo Updates in the Ferromagnetic State of the Doped SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Juntaro Fujii, Kazuki Yamamoto, Akihisa Koga
abstract: We investigate the sampling efficiency in a segment-based continuous-time hybridization-expansion quantum Monte Carlo solver within dynamical mean-field theory for the doped SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model. Focusing on the low-temperature and strong-coupling regime, where a ferromagnetic state appears upon hole doping away from one-third filling, we compare several update schemes. Adding the double-flip update to the basic local update yields the smallest integrated autocorrelation time of the majority-flavor occupation in the ferromagnetic regime, whereas adding the flavor-permutation update is the most effective in the paramagnetic regime. We further clarify the origin of this difference by analyzing the characteristic occupation changes caused by accepted updates.
summary: This work analyzes the efficiency of various Monte Carlo update schemes for simulating the doped SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model using DMFT and CT-HYB. By calculating the integrated autocorrelation time, the authors determine that the optimal update depends critically on the magnetic phase: double-flip updates are best for the ferromagnetic state, while flavor-permutation updates excel in the paramagnetic state. This highlights that understanding the physics of the accepted updates, rather than just acceptance ratios, is key to improving sampling algorithms.
main_problem: The study investigates the sampling efficiency of various update schemes within a Quantum Monte Carlo solver applied to the doped SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model.
main_result: The double-flip update is most efficient in the ferromagnetic state, while the flavor-permutation update is superior in the paramagnetic state, demonstrating that the nature of the required configuration change dictates the optimal update scheme.
method: The authors compare different Monte Carlo update schemes by calculating the integrated autocorrelation time ($\tau_{int}$) of the majority-flavor occupation, relating it to the variance of the MC average.
model_or_system: The system is the doped SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model on a hypercubic lattice. The problem is mapped onto an effective impurity problem solved using the Continuous-Time Hybridization-Expansion Quantum Monte Carlo (CT-HYB) method within Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT).
key_observables: Integrated autocorrelation time ($\tau_{int}$) of the majority-flavor occupation, flavor-resolved particle densities ($n_\sigma$), and the magnitude of occupation changes ($\Delta x$).
important_parameters: Low-temperature and strong-coupling regime; specific simulation parameters used were $T/D = 0.005$ and $U/D = 300$.
main_assumptions: The variance of the MC average is approximated as $\text{Var}(\langle X \rangle_{MC}) \simeq 2\tau_{int}(X) / N_{MCS}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of $\tau_{int}$ for different updates in FM and PM states, alongside probability distributions of occupation changes ($\Delta x$) caused by accepted updates.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the model and the CT-HYB/DMFT framework, compares three update schemes (simple, simple+flavor-permutation, simple+double-flip) by analyzing $\tau_{int}$ in both FM and PM regimes, and concludes by analyzing the mechanism—the characteristic scale of configuration changes—that dictates efficiency.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the rigorous analysis of sampling efficiency and the development of specialized update algorithms (like double-flip) are highly relevant to developing robust numerical techniques for strongly correlated quantum systems, which share methodological overlap with quantum simulation approaches.
